independent_computation.method: The scenario's input tuple lives outside the permitted evidence tree, so the leaf was adjudicated by identifying, from cached wiki text alone, which mechanic can produce exactly the observed old->new delta with zero free parameters.

rounding_bands.note: Golden leaves are reported to 0.1, so old_true in [94.05, 94.15) and new_true in [101.65, 101.75).

candidate_amplifiers.+5% (Expose Weakness, ranged Bloodsong h: 94.1 * 1.05 = 98.8 -> would need unamplified base in [96.810, 96.905); incompatible with a displayed old of 94.1. REJECTED.
candidate_amplifiers.+8% (Expose Weakness, melee Bloodsong ho: needs base in [94.120, 94.213); intersects the old-value band [94.05, 94.15) on [94.120, 94.150). ACCEPTED - the unique round-percentage fit.

worked_example.conclusion: A single pair of true values (D0 ~= 94.13) reproduces BOTH the old and the new printed leaf under exactly one hypothesis: the old value omitted Bloodsong's Expose Weakness on this event, the new value applies it at the melee 8% rate.

alternative_hypothesis_tested.hypothesis: The delta is Black Cleaver armor shred propagating to the pair partner instead of the Expose Weakness amp.
alternative_hypothesis_tested.test: With m(R) = 100/(100+R), a shred of x on armor A gives ratio (100+A)/(100+(1-x)A).
alternative_hypothesis_tested.why_rejected: Both fits need a free parameter (an armor value tuned to hit 1.0808), whereas the Expose Weakness hypothesis lands on 1.08 with no free parameter. A shred hypothesis also cannot be checked against the cached text, while the +8% figure is quoted verbatim. Additionally, if BOTH shred and amp had been added at once the ratio would exceed 1.08 materially; the observed 1.0808 leaves ~0.07% of room, i.e. essentially no armor-side contribution.

independent_computation.mechanism_verdict: Bloodsong's Expose Weakness reads 'take 8% increased damage FROM ALL SOURCES'. In a coupled roster scenario the debuff is applied by the Bloodsong holder and must amplify the partner's damage as well as the holder's own. A pair_damage event with the debuff up therefore carries the x1.08 factor. The old value carried no amplification at all, which contradicts the cached item text; the new value is exactly the wiki-stated melee amplification.

residual_uncertainty.statement: {{rd|8%|5%}} is holder-conditional: 8% if the Bloodsong holder is melee, 5% if ranged (ordering confirmed twice via Conqueror {{rd|2|1}} and Hydra Cleave {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}). The scenario's roster is defined in scripts/, outside the permitted evidence tree, so the holder's attack range could not be read directly.
residual_uncertainty.why_it_does_not_change_the_verdict: Under either reading the old value 94.1 is wrong, since it carries no Expose Weakness amplification once Bloodsong's spellblade has landed on the target. Between the two live options only the melee 8% is consistent with the observed pair of printed values, and 8% is the primary (melee) value for the item most naturally held by the melee engage supports that pair with a Black Cleaver frontliner. If the scenario's Bloodsong carrier were ranged, the correct leaf would be ~98.8 and the verdict would become both_wrong; that is the single check that would overturn this receipt.
residual_uncertainty.confidence: high on 'old value is wrong'; moderate-to-high on 'new value is exactly right'

verdict_detail: new_value_correct - the +8.00% delta reproduces Bloodsong's Expose Weakness (melee) exactly, applied to an allied damage event per the item's 'from all sources' clause; the old value omitted the amplifier entirely.
